messages:
anya: Heads-up — I merged the initial gateway rule for header-driven model aliasing but hit two edgecases: quota backpressure and alias compatibility. Thoughts?

devon: saw that. quick recap?

anya: rule is basically: if X-Tenant-Model == "assistant-v2" prefer alias "assistant-latest" but pin to tenant-version if header present. pasted snippet in PR.

sam: can you paste the rule here?

anya: sure:
```json
{
  "match": [{ "header": "X-Tenant-Model", "equals": "assistant-v2" }],
  "action": { "alias": "assistant-latest", "pin_header": "X-Tenant-Version", "soft_pin": true }
}
```

maria: soft_pin true is good for rollouts but we need compatibility constraints. some tenants will request "assistant-v2" but only support int8 quantized variants. we should annotate alias with capability matrix.

kevin: +1. We should have rule evaluation bailouts: if alias is incompatible with tenant capabilities then follow fallback chain instead of erroring. ops-bot: route_select.count++

devon: how do we discover tenant capabilities? headers? tenant profile in the control plane?

maria: we have tenant headers like X-Tenant-Capabilities: "quant:int8,kvcache:yes" but accuracy is low. better to surface recent inference telemetry (failed requests due to model mismatch) as signal.

sam: proposal: during routing, run capability-check step: compare alias.required_capabilities vs tenant.capabilities (header OR cached profile). if mismatch, try alias.fallbacks (listed in alias metadata) and increment telemetry counter pin_failure.rate.

anya: agree. also need quota/backpressure behavior: if tenant is over quota for dedicated pool, should gateway automatically route to cheaper hosted variant? We had a customer asking for that.

kevin: that's risky without explicit policy. We should support graceful downgrade with opt-in header: X-Allow-Degraded-Model: true. Otherwise return 429 or fallback to a pinned variant.

maria: UX in console needs to show effective decision: which model was picked and why (match, capability, quota). right now console shows only requested alias and final model id. Add columns: "decision_reason" and "fallback_chain_used".

devon: telemetry names to add: routing.decision_reason, routing.fallback_chain, routing.pin_failure, routing.quota_routed_to_hosted. these should be tags on span.

sam: example rollout policy config suggestion (console-friendly):
```yaml
rollout_policy:
  soft_pin: true
  allow_degrade_header: X-Allow-Degraded-Model
  capability_check: true
  fallback_order: ["assistant-compat", "assistant-hosted"]
```

anya: nice. small nit: fallback_order should be evaluated in context of cost SLA and tenant tier. e.g., enterprise tenants prefer dedicated fallback over hosted even if cost higher.

kevin: so fallback resolution needs policy precedence: explicit route override > tenant tier mapping > global default. implementable as short-circuit eval.

maria: for console rollout UX, add a toggle to simulate a tenant header and preview routing decisions with telemetry estimates (expected cost delta, expected p99 latency). helps PMs sanity-check.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: routed-rules-service v1.8.2 deployed to staging at 2024-11-18T09:12:00Z

devon: action items:
- annotate alias metadata with required_capabilities and fallback list (maria)
- add capability-check step + telemetry counters (sam)
- add X-Allow-Degraded-Model opt-in header and gate (kevin)
- console columns + simulation UX (anya + product)

anya: assigning tasks in the PR. I'll update the gateway evaluator to emit routing.decision_reason with values {match,capability_mismatch,quota_fallback,policy_override}. Also will add a compact explain field in logs: "pick=assistant-hosted(compat),reason=quota"

maria: one more: when pin_header present but tenant version unknown, treat as soft_pin default to alias and emit pin_uncertain metric. keeps rollouts observable.

sam: sounds good. will wire metrics to observability and add alert if pin_failure.rate > 0.5% for any top-50 tenant.

kevin: cool. if nobody objects I'll merge the follow-up PR with the capability-check stub tomorrow. :thumbsup:

anya: no objections. merging in the morning. thanks all!
